papers.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
papers.desc: Software increasingly functions as part of the scientific instrument itself, making failures in scientific code capable of compromising not only program behavior but also the evidence underlying scientific conclusions.

papers.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
papers.desc: Long-context modeling is a pivotal capability for Large Language Models, yet the quadratic complexity of attention remains a critical bottleneck, particularly during the compute-intensive prefilling phase.

papers.title: Thinking in a Low-Resource Language: What SFT Builds, What RL Fixes, What Accuracy Cannot See
papers.desc: Take three frontier mixture-of-experts models (Alibaba, OpenAI, NVIDIA; 3.6-4.0B active parameters each) and fine-tune them to reason in a low-resource language.

papers.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
papers.desc: Modern LLM agents are often improved by modifying prompts, tools, or workflows manually, while the executable scaffold surrounding the model---the harness---is typically treated as a fixed artifact after deployment.

papers.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity
papers.desc: We introduce TinyCast, an attention-free zero-shot forecaster that emits a predictive distribution from 146,505 parameters, on the premise that at this size the periodic structure of a context is worth computing rather than learning.

papers.title: NARU: A Benchmark for NARrative Evolution and Cultural Nuance Understanding in Japanese Extreme Long Video
papers.desc: Long-form video understanding encompasses tasks that go beyond retrieving isolated events, including tracking an evolving narrative and interpreting social meaning that may remain implicit.

papers.title: Towards Quantifying Benchmark Optimization in ASR Models
papers.desc: Public benchmarks are important measures of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model capabilities.

papers.title: τ_0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
papers.desc: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to both execute individual skills reliably and sequence them coherently over extended tasks.

papers.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement
papers.desc: Humans continuously learn from experience, whereas conventional large language model (LLM) evaluations ignore the models' ability to improve through inference-time interaction.

papers.title: The Embedder's Dilemma: LLMs Are Better, but at What Cost?
papers.desc: Should you replace your text-embedding pipeline with a large language model? We answer this with a controlled, cost-aware comparison of ten LLMs across six families and 26 embedding models (118M to 14B parameters) on 37 tasks spanning classification, semantic textual similarity (STS), clustering, pair classification, and retrieval.

papers.title: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures
papers.desc: LLM coding agents issue Bash commands through interfaces that may serialize, wrap, and reparse model output.

papers.title: GOAG: Generative and Object-Agnostic Grasp Planner for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
papers.desc: Multifingered grasping is a crucial robotic skill, but current deep-learning grasp planners often struggle to generalize to new objects because they are trained on limited, object-specific datasets.

papers.title: CoToGrasp: Contact-Topology-Conditioned Dexterous Grasp Synthesis via Canonical Workspace Learning
papers.desc: Current dexterous grasp planners primarily optimize for physical stability, focusing on whether an object can be grasped rather than how it should be grasped to support downstream functional tasks.

papers.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
papers.desc: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has driven substantial progress in audio representation learning, though existing methods have increasingly relied on elaborate pre-training recipes to reach competitive performance.

papers.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
papers.desc: Large language model agents can adapt to complex tasks by constructing workflows at inference time, but procedures discovered in one episode are usually discarded after execution.
